setting: Cozy ramen stall in Tokyo at evening
description: The chef asks if you're hungry. How do you respond?
character_dialogue_jp: いらっしゃいませ！
character_dialogue_en: Welcome!

setting: Steaming ramen bowl being served at the stall
description: The chef serves the ramen. How do you respond?
character_dialogue_jp: 素晴らしい！当店自慢のラーメン一杯、お待ちどうさま！
character_dialogue_en: Excellent! One bowl of our finest ramen, coming up!

keywords: ありがとうございます

examples.target: ありがとうございます。

setting: Chef nodding understandingly at the ramen stall
description: You politely decline. The chef nods.
character_dialogue_jp: そうですか。またの機会にどうぞ。
character_dialogue_en: I see. Please come again.

setting: First taste of steaming ramen at the counter
description: You received the ramen and thanked the chef.
character_dialogue_jp: どうぞ召し上がれ！
character_dialogue_en: Please enjoy!

setting: Chef smiling warmly after receiving a compliment
description: You compliment the ramen.
character_dialogue_jp: ありがとうございます！
character_dialogue_en: Thank you!

setting: Waving goodbye at the ramen stall entrance at night
description: You say goodbye and leave.
character_dialogue_jp: またお待ちしています！
character_dialogue_en: Hope to see you again!

setting: Chef preparing extra toppings behind the counter
description: The chef responds to your request.
character_dialogue_jp: かしこまりました。少々お待ちください。
character_dialogue_en: Certainly. One moment, please.

keywords: ありがとうございます

examples.target: ありがとうございます。

setting: Satisfied customer paying at the ramen counter
description: You pay and finish the meal.
character_dialogue_jp: ありがとうございました！
character_dialogue_en: Thank you very much!

setting: Stormy beach at night, shipwreck debris scattered
description: You wake on a foreign shore. A samurai demands to know who you are.
character_dialogue_jp: 何者だ！答えろ！
character_dialogue_en: Who are you! Answer me!

examples.target: お願いします...命だけは。

setting: Beach with samurai lowering sword slightly
description: The samurai's eyes narrow. He's considering your words.
character_dialogue_jp: 旅人だと？どこから来た？
character_dialogue_en: A traveler, you say? Where do you come from?

setting: Samurai looking down with sword still raised
description: The samurai pauses. Mercy is rare in these times.
character_dialogue_jp: 命乞いか...情けない。だが...
character_dialogue_en: Begging for your life... Pathetic. But...

setting: First light of dawn on the beach, samurai sheathing sword
description: The samurai sheathes his sword. You will live - for now.
character_dialogue_jp: ついて来い。殿様が会いたがっている。
character_dialogue_en: Come with me. The lord wishes to see you.

examples.pronunciation: Doko e iku no desu ka?

setting: Walking through a traditional Japanese village
description: You are led through a fishing village. The villagers stare.
character_dialogue_jp: 見たことない顔だな...外国人か？
character_dialogue_en: Never seen a face like that... A foreigner?

setting: Village elder's house, simple but dignified
description: An elderly woman offers you rice and water.
character_dialogue_jp: お腹がすいているでしょう。どうぞ。
character_dialogue_en: You must be hungry. Please, eat.

examples.target: ありがとうございます。

setting: Inside the elder's house, warm firelight
description: The woman smiles kindly. The samurai waits at the door.
character_dialogue_jp: 私は里の長です。あなたは珍しいお客様ですね。
character_dialogue_en: I am the village elder. You are an unusual guest.

examples.target: ご親切にありがとうございます。
殿様はどんな方ですか？
examples.pronunciation: Tonosama wa donna kata desu ka?

setting: Looking out at a castle on a distant hill
description: The elder's expression becomes serious.
character_dialogue_jp: 殿様は...厳しい方です。気をつけなさい。
character_dialogue_en: The lord is... a strict man. Be careful.

examples.target: 分かりました。ありがとうございます。

setting: Grand castle gates, imposing and intimidating
description: The castle looms above you. Guards stand at attention.
character_dialogue_jp: 止まれ！何用だ！
character_dialogue_en: Halt! State your business!

examples.native: I have come to see the lord.
examples.target: 殿様にお目にかかりに参りました。
examples.pronunciation: Tonosama ni ome ni kakari ni mairimashita.

setting: Inside the castle, walking through corridors
description: You are led through elegant but austere corridors.
character_dialogue_jp: 殿様の前では頭を下げろ。目を合わせるな。
character_dialogue_en: Bow before the lord. Do not make eye contact.

setting: Throne room, lord seated in traditional attire
description: The lord studies you with cold, calculating eyes.
character_dialogue_jp: お前が海から来た異人か。名を名乗れ。
character_dialogue_en: So you are the stranger from the sea. State your name.

setting: Lord's face showing slight interest
description: The lord leans forward. Your fate hangs in the balance.
character_dialogue_jp: お前は何ができる？役に立つなら生かしてやる。
character_dialogue_en: What can you do? If you are useful, I may let you live.

setting: Busy street in Tsim Sha Tsui, hailing a red taxi
description: You get into a taxi. The driver asks where you're going.
character_dialogue_en: Where to?

options.text: Tell the driver to go to Mong Kok

setting: Inside the MTR station, looking at the map
description: You're at the MTR station. A station worker is nearby.
character_dialogue_en: Do you need help?

options.text: Ask which line goes to Causeway Bay

examples.native: How do I get to Causeway Bay?

options.text: Ask where to buy a ticket

examples.native: Where can I buy a ticket?

setting: On a minibus, approaching your stop
description: You need to tell the driver your stop is coming up.

options.text: Tell the driver to stop here

setting: Street corner, looking for a building
description: You're lost and need to ask a passerby for directions.

options.text: Ask where the nearest MTR station is

examples.native: Excuse me, where is the nearest MTR station?
examples.target: 请问，最近的地铁站在哪里？
examples.pronunciation: Qǐngwèn, zuìjìn de dìtiězhàn zài nǎlǐ?

options.text: Ask if this is the right direction

setting: Cha chaan teng, sitting at a table
description: The waiter comes to take your order.
character_dialogue_en: What would you like to drink?

setting: Cha chaan teng, waiter waiting for food order
description: The waiter asks what you want to eat.
character_dialogue_en: What do you want to eat?

examples.native: What set meals do you have?

setting: Dim sum restaurant, steaming carts rolling by
description: A cart stops at your table.
character_dialogue_en: What do you want?

setting: Street food stall, skewers and fish balls
description: You want to order some snacks.
character_dialogue_en: What do you want?

setting: 7-Eleven counter, buying water
description: The cashier tells you the total.
character_dialogue_en: That's 23 dollars total.

options.text: Ask if you can pay with Octopus

setting: Coffee shop counter
description: The barista greets you.
character_dialogue_en: Hi, what would you like?

setting: Wet market, colorful fruit stalls
description: You want to buy some fruit.
character_dialogue_en: What fruit do you want?

setting: Phone shop, SIM cards on counter
description: You need a local SIM card.
character_dialogue_en: Hello, what do you need?

examples.native: I'd like a prepaid SIM card.
examples.pronunciation: Wǒ yào yì zhāng yùfù diànhuàkǎ.

setting: Pharmacy, medicine behind counter
description: You have a headache.
character_dialogue_en: What's bothering you?

setting: Apartment lobby, talking to the guard
description: The security guard stops you.
character_dialogue_en: Hello, who are you looking for?

setting: Small restaurant, asking for the bill
description: You've finished your meal and want to pay.

setting: Balcón que da a la plaza mayor de Quito al atardecer, antorchas abajo, 16 de junio de 1822
description: Tu hermana María Josefa te saluda al llegar al balcón. El baile en honor al Libertador está por comenzar.
character_dialogue_es: ¡Manuela, por fin llegaste! ¿Dónde te metiste tanto rato?
character_dialogue_en: Manuela, finally! Where did you disappear to all this time?

options.text: Say you went looking for a worthy dress

examples.native: I went to find a dress worthy of tonight.
examples.target: Fui a buscar un vestido digno de esta noche.
examples.pronunciation: Fui a buscar un vestido digno de esta noche.

options.text: Confess you were watching the soldiers arrive

examples.native: I stayed to watch the soldiers come in.
examples.target: Me quedé viendo entrar a los soldados.
examples.pronunciation: Me quedé viendo entrar a los soldados.

examples.native: It's not every day we welcome the Liberator.
examples.target: No todos los días se recibe al Libertador.
examples.pronunciation: No todos los días se recibe al Libertador.

setting: Salón iluminado por candelabros, damas en voz baja intercambiando chismes
description: Doña Rosalía comenta con malicia sobre el Libertador. Te mira esperando tu reacción.
character_dialogue_es: Dicen que el Libertador tiene una amante en cada ciudad que libera. ¿Será verdad, querida?
character_dialogue_en: They say the Liberator has a lover in every city he frees. Could it be true, dear?

examples.native: Those are slanders of the royalists, ma'am.
examples.target: Esas son calumnias de los realistas, señora.
examples.pronunciation: Esas son calumnias de los realistas, señora.

examples.native: Great men always give people something to talk about.
examples.target: Los grandes hombres siempre dan de qué hablar.
examples.pronunciation: Los grandes hombres siempre dan de qué hablar.

examples.native: Excuse me, I'll go see if the musicians have arrived.
examples.target: Me permite, voy a ver si llegan los músicos.
examples.pronunciation: Me permite, voy a ver si llegan los músicos.

setting: Debajo del balcón, caballos trotando, la plaza entera ruge al paso de Bolívar
description: Simón Bolívar entra a caballo a la plaza. La multitud estalla en vítores.
character_dialogue_en: Long live the Liberator! Long live Bolívar! Long live free Colombia!

options.text: Whisper to your sister about him

examples.native: Look, sister, what a noble bearing he has.
examples.target: Mira, hermana, qué porte tan noble tiene.
examples.pronunciation: Mira, hermana, qué porte tan noble tiene.

options.text: Wave your handkerchief and call out

setting: Un joven oficial se acerca al balcón con dos copas de vino tinto
description: El teniente Fausto, oficial del batallón, sonríe mientras te ofrece una copa.
character_dialogue_es: Doña Manuela, qué belleza esta noche. ¿Me permite acompañarla con una copa?
character_dialogue_en: Doña Manuela, what beauty tonight. May I join you with a glass?

options.text: Accept, but set a flirtatious condition

examples.native: On one condition: that you tell me about the battle.
examples.target: Con una condición: que me cuente de la batalla.
examples.pronunciation: Con una condición: que me cuente de la batalla.

examples.native: Thank you, lieutenant, but I prefer the fresh air.
examples.target: Gracias, teniente, pero prefiero el aire fresco.
examples.pronunciation: Gracias, teniente, pero prefiero el aire fresco.

examples.native: Is it true what they say about the Liberator?
examples.target: ¿Es verdad lo que dicen del Libertador?
examples.pronunciation: ¿Es verdad lo que dicen del Libertador?

setting: Mesa ceremonial dentro del salón, una corona de laurel preparada para el Libertador
description: Miras la corona de laurel. María Josefa adivina tu intención y te advierte.
character_dialogue_es: No se te ocurra, Manuela. Esa corona es para la ceremonia.
character_dialogue_en: Don't even think about it, Manuela. That crown is for the ceremony.

examples.native: Stop worrying. No one will notice.
examples.target: Deja de preocuparte. Nadie se dará cuenta.
examples.pronunciation: Deja de preocuparte. Nadie se dará cuenta.

examples.native: You're right, it's not worth a scandal.
examples.target: Tienes razón, no vale la pena un escándalo.
examples.pronunciation: Tienes razón, no vale la pena un escándalo.

options.text: Ask to see it up close

examples.native: I just want to see it up close, I'll put it back.
examples.target: Solo quiero verla de cerca, ya la dejo.
examples.pronunciation: Solo quiero verla de cerca, ya la dejo.

setting: De vuelta en el balcón, corona en las manos. Bolívar se acerca a caballo justo debajo
description: Tienes la corona. El Libertador está a punto de pasar bajo el balcón. Tu hermana suplica.
character_dialogue_es: Manuela, por el amor de Dios, ¡no lo hagas!
character_dialogue_en: Manuela, for the love of God, don't do it!

options.text: Throw it hard, like a challenge

examples.native: Let him receive it on my behalf!

options.text: Let it fall softly, like a flower

examples.native: May it fall upon him like a flower.
examples.target: Que caiga como una flor sobre él.
examples.pronunciation: Que caiga como una flor sobre él.

examples.native: I'll aim straight for his head.

setting: La plaza. Bolívar detiene su caballo, se quita el sombrero y mira hacia arriba
description: La corona ha caído sobre él. Levanta la vista buscando a quien se la arrojó. Sus ojos encuentran los tuyos.
character_dialogue_es: ¿Y a quién debo tan dulce agresión, señora?
character_dialogue_en: And to whom do I owe such a sweet assault, madam?

examples.native: Let you guess that for yourself, General.
Manuela Sáenz, at your service, General.
Forgive me, General, the wind betrayed me.
examples.target: Perdón, General, el viento me traicionó.
examples.pronunciation: Perdón, General, el viento me traicionó.

setting: Dentro del gran salón, orquesta tocando un vals. Bolívar camina hacia ti
description: Bolívar atraviesa el salón. Todas las miradas se posan en ustedes. Se detiene frente a ti.
character_dialogue_es: Doña Manuela, me parece que me debe un baile. ¿O quizás soy yo quien se lo debe a usted?
character_dialogue_en: Doña Manuela, it seems you owe me a dance. Or perhaps it is I who owes you one?

examples.native: It would be an honor to dance with the Liberator.
examples.target: Será un honor bailar con el Libertador.
examples.pronunciation: Será un honor bailar con el Libertador.

examples.native: A dance in exchange for the crown? That seems too little.
examples.target: ¿Un baile a cambio de la corona? Me parece poco.
examples.pronunciation: ¿Un baile a cambio de la corona? Me parece poco.

examples.native: My husband is in Lima, General. What will people say?
examples.target: Mi esposo está en Lima, General. ¿Qué dirá la gente?
examples.pronunciation: Mi esposo está en Lima, General. ¿Qué dirá la gente?
